bands.1:
Twotide Atoll is a ring of white sand in a blue lagoon. The sun is blazing. Mo fries an egg on the hot deck.

"There is a 92 per cent chance of sunburn," says Tully.

The tide comes in and out twice a day. At low tide, a sandbar leads to a dark sea cave.

Two Duettle hatchlings argue on a rock.

"We found a boat," says one.

"No, the boat found US," says the other.

"Why did the turtle cross the beach?" asks Mo. "To get to the other tide!"

Everyone groans. A Sidlewink hides in the sand.

At the back of the cave is a gold door. The sign says, "ECHO STUDIO. SHHH. GENIUS AT WORK."

"He always does a squeaky voice for animals," says Wren, so quietly that only you hear.

A tall man walks out of the palm trees. He has bare feet and a cloak made of old sails. A tiny bat hangs from his hat.

"A strange boat arrives," says the man. "Narra the Teller does not trust it."

"Trust it," squeaks the bat. "Trust it."

"That is Echobat," says Narra. "It repeats things."

"Why do you talk about yourself like a book?" asks Zed.

"Everybody is in a story," says Narra. "But whose story is it?"

He tells you about Maxx's video. In it, Maxx scoops up turtle hatchlings. They squeak with joy.

"That is Maxx's story," says Narra. "Here is the hatchlings' story. A net came down. They did not squeak. They screamed."

"Will you help us?" you ask.

"Win Narra's badge, Captain," he says. "Then we will see."

That night, Narra sits beside you.

"Once, Echobat flew into that cave," he says. "It came out different."

Echobat lands on your knee. It speaks in Maxx's voice.

"Smash that heart button!" it squeaks. "Bring the nets. Tomorrow we get the twins."

On the rock, the two Duettles stop arguing.

The tide here comes in twice a day, fast as a bath, and rushes out again just as fast. At low tide, a sandbar rises out of the lagoon and stretches to a dark sea cave at the end of the atoll. At high tide, the cave mouth vanishes underwater.

"We found a boat," squeaks one.

The groan is so loud that a Sidlewink buries itself in the sand.

Zed scans the cave with his binoculars. "Found it," he says. At the very back, half-hidden by dripping rock, is a gold padded door. A sign hangs above it: "ECHO STUDIO. SHHH. GENIUS AT WORK."

"He always does a squeaky voice for animals," Wren mutters, staring at the cave.

Then a deep, slow voice rolls across the beach.

"A strange boat arrives at Twotide," says the voice. "Its crew looks hot, lost and badly fed. Narra the Teller does not trust them. Not yet."

"That is Echobat," says Narra the Teller. "Echobat repeats the last word of everything. "

"Everything," squeaks the bat. "Everything."

"That is Maxx's story," says Narra. "Now Narra will tell you the hatchlings' story. They were racing for the sea, as hatchlings do. A net came down. They did not squeak with joy. Narra heard them from the beach. They screamed."

"So the happy noises in the video..." Indi begins.

"Are not theirs," says Narra.

"Will you help us?" you ask.

Narra looks at you for a long time. "Narra the Teller helps only those who can tell whose story is being told. Win his badge, Captain. Then we will see."

"See," says Echobat. "See."

The little bat flutters down onto your knee and opens its mouth.

"Smash that heart button like it owes you money!" it squeaks, in Maxx's voice. Then, still in Maxx's voice: "Bring the nets. Tomorrow we record the twins."

Twotide Atoll is a ring of white sand around a lagoon so blue that it looks fake. The sun is blazing, the palm trees are lazy, and the deck of the Soggy Biscuit is hot enough to fry an egg on, which Mo immediately tries.

"There's a 92 per cent chance of sunburn," says Tully, smearing zinc across her nose. "And a hundred per cent chance that egg is now part of the boat."

Twice a day the tide comes in, as fast as a bath filling, and twice a day it rushes out again. At low tide, a sandbar rises out of the lagoon and runs all the way to a dark sea cave at the far end of the atoll; at high tide, the cave mouth vanishes completely underwater, as if it had never been there.

The beach is crawling with Creatures. A Whoshell swaps its shell for a bigger one and scuttles back as if it were a completely different crab. A Wherrow circles once overhead, checks the angle of the sun and sets off across the ocean without so much as glancing at a map. Two Duettle hatchlings are arguing on a rock.

"We found a boat," squeaks one.

"No, the boat found US," squeaks the other. "And it was terrifying."

Mo serves lunch: coconut-and-anchovy smoothies, each with the fried egg balanced on top. "Why did the turtle cross the beach?" he asks. "To get to the other tide!"

The groan is so loud and so long that a Sidlewink buries itself in the sand in disgust.

Zed is scanning the atoll with his binoculars. "Found it," he says. At the very back of the sea cave, half-hidden by dripping rock, is a padded gold door. A gold sign hangs above it: "ECHO STUDIO. SHHH. GENIUS AT WORK."

"A recording studio," says Indi, "in a cave. Of course it is."

"He always does a squeaky voice for animals," Wren mutters, staring at the cave, so quietly that only you hear.

Then a voice rolls across the beach, deep and slow, like a storyteller beside a campfire.

"A strange boat arrives at Twotide," says the voice. "Its crew looks hot, lost and badly fed. Narra the Teller does not trust them. Not yet."

A tall, barefoot man strolls out from under the palms. His cloak is stitched from hundreds of old sails, each patch printed with a different story. A tiny bat hangs upside down from the brim of his straw hat.

"Narra the Teller welcomes you," says Narra the Teller, "but only a little."

"Little," squeaks the bat. "Little."

"That is Echobat," Narra explains. "Echobat repeats the last word of everything. It is very bad at keeping secrets."

"Secrets," says Echobat. "Secrets."

"Why are you talking about yourself like you're in a book?" asks Zed.

"Because everybody is in a story," says Narra the Teller. "The only question is, whose story is it?"

He sits cross-legged on the sand and tells you about Maxx's newest video, "Maxx Saves the Happy Hatchlings!" In it, Maxx scoops up baby turtles in the moonlight, and they chirp and squeak with joy as he carries them away. It has nine million views.

"That is Maxx's story," says Narra. "Now Narra the Teller will tell you the hatchlings' story. They were racing for the sea, as hatchlings do. A net came down. They did not squeak with joy. Narra heard them from the beach. They screamed."

Indi frowns. "Then whose squeaks are in the video?"

Narra does not answer. He only looks, for a long moment, at the padded gold door at the back of the cave.

"Will you help us?" you ask.

Narra looks at you for a long time, as if he is deciding what kind of character you are. "Narra the Teller helps only those who can tell whose story is being told. Win his badge, Captain. Then we will see."

"See," says Echobat. "See."

That night, at low tide, the crew sits on the beach and watches gold light leak out of the cave. Narra sits down beside you, quieter than before.

"Narra has one more story," he says. "One night, Echobat flew into that cave. Narra waited on the sand until the tide came in. In the morning, Echobat came out, but Echobat came out different."

The little bat flutters down onto your knee. It opens its mouth.

"Smash that heart button like it owes you money!" it squeaks, in Maxx's voice.

Then, still in Maxx's voice: "Bring the nets. Tomorrow we record the twins."

On the rock, the two Duettles stop arguing.
